title: Lemonite: identification of regulatory metabolites through data-driven, interpretable integration of transcriptomics and metabolomics data
abstract: Biological regulation emerges from coordinated interactions between genes, proteins, and metabolites; yet, despite their central regulatory potential, metabolites remain largely absent from genome-wide gene regulatory network inference. Current transcriptomics-metabolomics integration approaches are either limited by poor interpretability or constrained by incomplete prior knowledge, preventing the systematic identification of regulatory metabolites. Here, we present Lemonite, a data-driven and interpretable framework for integrating bulk transcriptomics and metabolomics data to uncover regulatory metabolites acting on gene modules. Lemonite extends module network inference to jointly associate transcription factors and metabolites with coexpressed gene programs, without requiring prior differential analysis or complete metabolite annotation. To contextualize predictions, we construct a comprehensive gene-metabolite knowledge graph integrating over 370,000 metabolite-gene and 2.1 million protein-protein interactions. Applied to glioblastoma and inflammatory bowel disease cohorts, Lemonite identifies over 50 functionally coherent gene modules per disease, revealing established and previously uncharacterized metabolite-gene regulatory relationships. In glioblastoma, myo-inositol and phosphatidylcholines, together with IRF6, regulate mesenchymal-like immune programs, which upon integration with single-cell transcriptomics are primarily expressed in tumor-associated macrophages and monocytes. In inflammatory bowel disease, regulatory metabolites are prioritized that change the expression of their predicted target genes in vitro. Together, Lemonite provides a principled framework to explore the genome-wide regulatory potential of the metabolome and to generate biologically interpretable, experimentally testable hypotheses from multi-omics data.

llm.novelty_zh: 将转录组与代谢组通过模块网络推断联合建模，无需先验差异分析或完整代谢物注释，即可识别作用于基因模块的调控代谢物，并结合基因-代谢物知识图谱增强可解释性。
llm.summary_zh: Lemonite 是一个面向批量转录组与代谢组数据的可解释整合框架，通过扩展模块网络推断，联合关联转录因子与代谢物和共表达基因模块，以发现调控性代谢物。作者构建了包含 37 万余条代谢物-基因关系与 210 万条蛋白互作的知识图谱，并在胶质母细胞瘤和炎症性肠病队列中给出可检验的假设，部分在体外实验中得到验证。该工作属于多组学基因调控网络推断，与虚拟细胞的扰动建模只有间接关系。
